summary: Modern databases have rapidly embedded AI and ML capabilities directly into their platforms, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference, embedding generation, and vector search. By 2026, vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search capabilities, driving platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB to natively integrate LLM pipelines, embedding models, and similarity search. The trend is converging toward general-purpose databases handling AI workloads that previously required purpose-built vector databases, with pgvector on PostgreSQL emerging as the default for most RAG workloads up to 50 million vectors.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI is Snowflake's fully managed AI service suite running natively in the AI Data Cloud. It includes Cortex LLM Functions for inference (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, TRANSLATE), Cortex Search for hybrid vector and keyword search, Cortex Analyst for natural language to SQL (text-to-SQL), and embedding generation via EMBED_TEXT functions. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates directly with Cortex AI, including pgvector support for vector similarity search, text-to-SQL, and generating embeddings within the same governed environment. Data never leaves Snowflake, preserving security and governance.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Mistral, Llama 3, Reka, Arctic, and other models via Cortex LLM Functions. Snowflake Postgres + Cortex AI enables text-to-SQL and embedding generation. External model integrations available via Cortex Fine-tuning and partner ecosystem.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits per token or per call depending on the function. Cortex Search has additional storage and query costs. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows Snowflake's compute credit model. Costs vary by model size and region; enterprise contracts may include negotiated rates.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute ML models directly in BigQuery using SQL, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, XGBoost, deep neural networks, and AutoML. BigQuery's Vertex AI integration enables remote model inference, embedding generation using text-embedding models, and vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function on embedding columns. BigQuery also supports LLM-powered features like ML.GENERATE_TEXT for calling Gemini models in-database and ML.EMBED_TEXT for generating embeddings without data movement.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Google Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini Flash) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT. Vertex AI model garden accessible from BigQuery for custom and foundation model inference. Supports PaLM 2 and third-party models via Vertex AI endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference billed per byte processed or per prediction depending on model type. VECTOR_SEARCH queries billed at standard BigQuery compute rates. Gemini model calls via ML.GENERATE_TEXT billed per character or token at Vertex AI rates. On-demand and flat-rate slot pricing available.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector similarity search directly to existing Postgres instances, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. It requires no new infrastructure, maintains the same security model and backup procedures, and handles up to 50 million vectors making it the recommended default for most RAG workloads in 2026. pgai is a complementary extension by Timescale that brings embedding generation and LLM inference directly into SQL, enabling AI workflows without leaving the database. Together they provide a full in-database AI stack on standard PostgreSQL.
databases.llm_integration: pgai integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and Ollama for embedding generation and LLM inference via SQL functions. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector integrates natively with Cortex AI. Supabase Vector and Neon both offer managed pgvector with additional LLM tooling. Works with any Postgres-compatible hosting provider.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Costs depend entirely on the PostgreSQL hosting provider (self-hosted is infrastructure cost only). Managed providers like Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, and Google Cloud SQL charge their standard Postgres pricing with no additional fee for pgvector. LLM API calls billed by the external provider per token.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.ai_feature: Aurora ML and Redshift ML with SageMaker and Bedrock integration
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables calling ML models hosted on Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock directly from Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL using SQL functions, allowing inference without data movement. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector for vector similarity search and embedding storage. Redshift ML uses AutoML via SageMaker Autopilot to create, train, and deploy ML models with SQL CREATE MODEL statements, and supports remote inference against SageMaker endpoints and Bedrock foundation models. Amazon Bedrock integration allows calling foundation models like Claude, Llama, and Titan directly from SQL in both Aurora and Redshift environments.
databases.llm_integration: Integration with Amazon Bedrock for access to Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama 3, Amazon Titan, Mistral, and Cohere models via SQL. SageMaker Autopilot for automated model training in Redshift ML. Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for embedding storage and retrieval paired with Bedrock for end-to-end RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference billed per invocation plus standard Aurora compute costs. Redshift ML model training billed via SageMaker Autopilot rates plus Redshift compute. Bedrock model calls billed per token at Bedrock rates. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional licensing cost beyond standard Aurora instance pricing. Data transfer between Aurora and SageMaker may incur additional charges.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI — MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an integrated AI platform combining MLflow for ML lifecycle management (experiment tracking, model registry, deployment), Mosaic AI for fine-tuning and serving foundation models, and DBRX as Databricks' own open-source LLM. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database built into the Lakehouse that automatically syncs with Delta Lake tables, enabling real-time vector similarity search. Unity Catalog governs all ML models and vector indexes. The platform supports RAG pipeline construction, LLM evaluation, and AI agent frameworks natively. pgvector integrates well with Databricks environments for teams using Postgres alongside the Lakehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for DBRX, Llama 3, Mixtral, and other open models via Mosaic AI Model Serving. Integration with external providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Azure OpenAI via AI Gateway. MLflow tracks experiments across all model types. LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations built-in for RAG and agent workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks billing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs) per workload type. Vector Search has separate DBU pricing based on index size and query volume. Model Serving billed per token for provisioned throughput or per DBU for pay-per-token endpoints. MLflow tracking is included at no additional cost. Enterprise pricing available with Unity Catalog governance included.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing vector embeddings alongside operational data in the same document database, eliminating the need for a separate vector store. It supports approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW indexes on embedding fields within Atlas collections, and can perform hybrid search combining vector similarity with MongoDB's full-text search and standard query filters in a single pipeline. Atlas Vector Search integrates with the Atlas Data Platform including Atlas Stream Processing and Atlas Search, enabling real-time AI applications. Pre-built integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Hugging Face simplify RAG pipeline construction.
databases.llm_integration: Integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Cohere, and Hugging Face for embedding generation and LLM inference. Native connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Atlas allows storing embeddings generated by any external model alongside source documents. No native in-database LLM inference; relies on external model providers.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included in MongoDB Atlas clusters with no separate licensing fee for the vector search capability itself. Costs scale with cluster tier (compute and storage). Vector index storage counts toward Atlas storage billing. Shared free tier (M0) supports limited vector search for prototyping. Dedicated clusters starting at M10 recommended for production vector workloads. Serverless Atlas instances also support vector search with consumption-based pricing.
